business_problem: Singapore Civil Defence Force needed a better way to prioritize fire safety inspections as urban density, new building uses, electric vehicles, battery systems, and other emerging risks made static compliance checks and officer judgment alone too slow and inconsistent for changing conditions.
solution_summary: Singapore Civil Defence Force worked with Accenture to turn years of inspection history and urban-risk data into an operational AI system for fire-safety regulation. The program consolidated inspection records and related operational data into iCore, a connected data foundation that acts as the shared intelligence layer for fire-safety teams. On top of that foundation, predictive analytics models surface risk signals and rank premises that are most likely to contain violations. Those scores are pushed into the Targeted Onsite Inspection Tool (TOIT), which replaces manual scheduling with data-driven planning for inspectors. Gen AI was then added to support research, interpretation, and inspection documentation so officers can use richer context while keeping human judgment and accountability in the loop. The result is a continuously learning regulatory workflow that improves as more inspections feed the common platform.
